chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about the patient who is unable to sit. He said, 'Let him pray while lying down, and let him place something on his forehead when he prostrates, for that suffices for him, and Allah will not burden a soul beyond its capacity.'

key_terms.يُجْزِي عَنْهُ: suffices for him / is accepted on his behalf

ai.seo_question: How should a patient who cannot sit perform their prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the practical methodology for *salat al-mudtir* (prayer of the compelled), emphasizing that prostration is indicated by a slight inclination of the head rather than full physical bowing. It reinforces the juristic principle of *la haraj* (no hardship), ensuring that the physical limitations of the ill do not invalidate the spiritual obligation of prayer.
